Gifts by budget

10 secondhand aviation gifts to consider before buying new

Secondhand gifts can offer character and value, particularly for readers, collectors, and history enthusiasts. The useful question is whether condition and authenticity can be assessed well enough for the intended gift. This list favors off-duty items over operational equipment with an unknown history.

By Pilot Gift Guide Updated 2026-10-20

How we choose our recommendations
In this guideThe ideasHow to chooseMore gift ideas

The ideas

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    Aviation memoir

    Choose a readable copy of a title they want. Check for missing pages, heavy annotations, and smells that may not appear in listing photographs.

  2. 2

    Aircraft history book

    A specialist subject can be more meaningful than a broad new gift book. Confirm the edition and whether photographs are reproduced clearly.

  3. 3

    Airline postcard collection

    Choose a focused set connected to an era or place. Ask whether cards are original, reproduced, written on, or altered.

  4. 4

    Display model

    Inspect photos of wings, landing gear, and antennas. Confirm the stand and box are included if those matter to the collector.

  5. 5

    Vintage aviation advertisement

    Check whether it is an original page or a modern print. Frame it as decor without overstating rarity or historical significance.

  6. 6

    Museum exhibition catalog

    An older catalog can recall a visit or interest. Verify the title and condition rather than assuming all museum publications are substantial books.

  7. 7

    Aircraft photograph

    Establish what is known about the image and its source. Do not add a confident date or identification that the seller cannot support.

  8. 8

    Aviation board game

    Confirm all pieces and instructions are present. Missing components can turn a charming gift into a project the recipient did not request.

  9. 9

    Model-building reference material

    Choose a subject matching an active project. Older references can be useful for historical interest while remaining separate from current operational guidance.

  10. 10

    Collector display accessory

    A used case or stand may offer value if it fits. Inspect dimensions, damage, and mounting details before arranging transport.

How to choose

Ask for clear photographs, dimensions, and an honest condition description. Check return terms and the delivered total. Avoid presenting reproductions as originals, and do not assume vintage technical publications are current references for flying. A clean, thoughtfully selected used item can stand on its own.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
